name: Hydrogen peroxide eye drops

card.summary: Putting hydrogen peroxide in the eyes to whiten them; reference sources warn that even 3 percent can injure the eye.
card.note: Associated with corneal injury; reference sources say concentrations as low as 3% can be dangerous for the eye.

quick.overview:
Some people have tried putting hydrogen peroxide solution in the eyes in the hope of whitening or cleaning them. It is a household antiseptic, not an ophthalmic product.

Reference sources warn that even 3 percent solution can be dangerous to the eye because oxygen is released inside it. No studies support the practice for appearance.
quick.mechanism: Hydrogen peroxide is an oxidising disinfectant that breaks down into water and oxygen. Contact lens systems use 3 percent peroxide with a catalytic disc that neutralises it before lenses go back in the eye.
quick.risks: Reference sources state that concentrations as low as 3% can be dangerous for the eye. Higher concentrations cause skin burns and react violently with organic material. Direct eye use is associated with corneal injury.

lead: Hydrogen peroxide eye drops refers to applying hydrogen peroxide solution directly to the eye, sometimes with the aim of whitening or cleansing it. It is not a medically recognised treatment for that purpose, and no published studies of it for appearance were found.

Household peroxide is typically 3 or 6 percent by weight. It is used as a surface disinfectant and, in neutralised form, for contact lens disinfection [1]. Reference sources warn that concentrations as low as 3% can be dangerous for the eye because oxygen is released within it [1].

paras: Consumer hydrogen peroxide is sold at 3 or 6 percent, with 30 percent common in laboratories and stronger grades far more hazardous [1]. Contact lenses are often disinfected in 3 percent peroxide, with a catalytic disc in the case that breaks it down before the lenses are reused [1]. Solutions up to 35 percent cause skin bubbling and pain, and concentrated solutions react violently with organic materials [1].
